eventMetadata.context_description:
**Forecast models from agencies including the Met Office, BBC Weather, and yr.no indicate a high of 25–26°C in Amsterdam on August 15, 2026, following the peak of a regional heatwave.** On August 13–14, the Netherlands recorded its fifth heatwave of the season, with national stations reaching 33–34°C and some southern locations approaching 36°C under a strong heat dome. By the 15th, a northwest airflow and increased cloud cover are expected to advect cooler maritime air, moderating daytime maxima.

Ensemble guidance shows the daily maximum centered near 25–26°C, with minor spread arising from the exact timing of any showers or breaks in cloud that could allow brief additional warming. The 27°C bin captures upside risk if subsidence or clearer skies persist longer than currently modeled. Lower outcomes (24°C or below) would require faster or stronger frontal passage. Market-implied probabilities align closely with this consensus, weighting the most likely bins while reflecting residual uncertainty in short-range model solutions. Updated KNMI or ECMWF runs over the next 12–24 hours will provide the clearest signal ahead of resolution.
